cases.title: Automatic Page Load Display of Current Weekday and Quote
cases.description: Verify that upon loading the web page, the application automatically determines the current day of the week from the local computer date and displays the correct weekday name in the span with data-testid='weekday' and the corresponding quote in the span with data-testid='phrase' without any user interaction.

cases.title: DOM Structure and Element Selection Verification
cases.description: Verify that the page structure includes the container div with data-testid='container', the heading with data-testid='heading', and the required span elements with data-testid='weekday' and data-testid='phrase', and that JavaScript executes on load to update their innerHTML properties properly.

opinions.feedback: The proposed cases adequately cover the requirements for automatic loading, correct element identifiers, and day-specific content mapping based on local date settings.

analysis.analysis: Requirement e2edev_bench_46-R-1 and e2edev_bench_46-R-2 define automatic, zero-interaction initialization upon page load. Testable behaviors include: reading the local computer's date to determine the current day of the week (Sunday through Saturday), updating the span element `data-testid='weekday'` with the correct day name, and updating the span element `data-testid='phrase'` with the predefined quote associated with that day. Boundaries and normal paths cover all seven days of the week mapping to their respective day names and quotes. Abnormal paths or edge cases include handling invalid or manipulated local dates, ensuring DOM elements (container div `data-testid='container'`, heading `data-testid='heading'`, and the two span elements) are correctly queried via data-testid, and verifying that innerHTML updates occur immediately without requiring user interaction or persistent storage.
